description: Capture a ransomware incident in a single pass: family / variant, observation date, affected scope, network indicators, malware-sample hashes, ransom note details, and attribution. Designed to be filled while triage is still ongoing.
name: Ransomware incident

structure.help: High-level facts about the incident. If you don't know all of these yet, fill what you can — the template can be edited as the response progresses.
structure.label: Incident overview

structure.help: Best-known label for the family — e.g. *LockBit*, *BlackCat (ALPHV)*, *Akira*. If your AV product gives a more specific variant, capture that. Leave blank if you genuinely don't know yet; better than guessing.
structure.label: Ransomware family / variant name

structure.help: When the encryption / extortion behaviour was first observed (not when the report was filed). ISO 8601 — e.g. `2026-04-25T03:42:00Z`.
structure.label: Date first observed

structure.default_content:
## What happened

_Brief description of the encryption / extortion event._

## Affected systems

- 

## Current status

_Containment, recovery, negotiation posture._
structure.help: Free-form Markdown — what happened, what's affected, what's the current status. Saved as an EventReport attached to the new event.
structure.label: Incident summary

structure.help: Roughly what was hit. Don't try to be exhaustive — capture representative items, full host inventories belong in the case-management system.
structure.label: Affected scope

structure.help: FQDN or short hostname of an affected machine. Use **+ Add another instance** for additional hosts.
structure.label: Affected hostname

structure.help: Username or email of an account where the encryption was observed. Helpful for correlating to the spearphish that delivered the loader, if any.
structure.label: Affected user

structure.help: C2 endpoints, leak-site URLs, payment-portal addresses. Anything reachable over the network.
structure.label: Network indicators

structure.help: Full URL. Defang if your tooling requires (`hxxp://`, `[.]`). One URL per entry; use **+ Add another instance** for more.
structure.label: C2 / leak-site URL

structure.help: Bare domain (no scheme, no path). Use only when you have the domain but not a full URL.
structure.label: C2 domain

structure.help: Resolves to a C2 endpoint at the time of observation. Note that ransomware C2 is often fast-flux — the IP today may not be the IP in a week.
structure.label: C2 destination IP

structure.help: If you have the loader / encryptor binary, capture its hashes here. The **File** object groups them so they correlate as a single sample.
structure.label: Malware sample

structure.help: At minimum, capture filename + SHA-256. MD5 / SHA-1 are useful for matching against legacy feeds.
structure.label: Sample (loader or encryptor)

relations.help_override: Filename as observed on the affected machine. Often randomised by ransomware loaders — capture what you saw.
Optional — helpful for matching legacy AV signatures.
Useful collision filter when only a partial hash is available.

structure.help: Information about the ransom itself — note, payment address, amount.
structure.label: Ransom demand

structure.help: Filename(s) of the ransom note dropped on affected systems — e.g. `README_FOR_DECRYPT.txt`. Commonly identical across the family.
structure.label: Ransom note filename

structure.help: If the demand specifies a Bitcoin address, capture it verbatim. One per entry.
structure.label: Bitcoin payment address

structure.help: Free-form — e.g. `2.5 BTC`, `$50,000 in Monero`, `unknown`. Captured as text because units vary.
structure.label: Ransom amount

structure.help: TLP for the report and any galaxy-cluster attribution you can support with evidence.
structure.label: Classification and attribution

structure.help: Pick one. Override the `tlp:amber` default if your analyst's TLP differs.
structure.label: TLP

structure.help: Pick the matching cluster from the *ransomware* galaxy. Distinct from the **Ransomware family / variant name** text field above — that's free-form, this is the curated cluster id.
structure.label: Ransomware family (galaxy)

structure.help: Optional. Many ransomware operations are run by named affiliates — only fill in if you have evidence beyond the family alone.
structure.label: Suspected threat actor

structure.content: **Follow-up:** ransomware reports almost always need updates. The free-text **Short incident summary** field above is intentionally narrow — write the detailed timeline, lessons learned, and IR steps in an *event report* on the resulting event, not in the template fields.
